It contains no\nwarrior code. The language itself is documented in `redcode/`, `guide.htm` and\n`icws94-standard.txt`.\n\n## Archetypes\n\n- **Imp.** `MOV 0, 1` copies itself one cell ahead forever.\n  - Imps are very hard to kill and kill almost nothing, so on their own they mostly tie.\n  - Several imps spaced CORESIZE/n apart and executed in turn form an *imp ring* or\n    *imp spiral*, which is sturdier.\n- **Stone (bomber).** A small loop that drops bombs (DAT to kill, SPL to slow) at a\n  fixed step through the core.\n  - It is small, fast and hard to find.\n  - The choice of step matters: it decides how evenly and how fast the core gets\n    covered.\n- **Paper (replicator).** Copies itself to new places, again and again, and spawns many\n  processes.\n  - Killing one copy does not kill the warrior, so DAT bombs alone rarely beat it.\n  - \"Silk\" papers copy with `SPL`/`MOV` pairs and post-increment pointers.\n- **Scanner.** Looks for non-empty cells (`SEQ`/`SNE`/`JMZ`), then attacks what it\n  found.\n  - Typical attacks: a few bombs, a carpet of `SPL 0` bombs that stuns the target, or a\n    switch into a core clear.\n  - A scanner has to avoid detecting itself, and its speed is measured in cells per\n    cycle (0.5c, 0.66c, ...).\n- **Core clear.** Overwrites the whole core in sequence, typically with SPL first\n  (stun), then DAT (kill).\n  - Clears are used to finish off stunned opponents. They are often the last phase of a\n    scanner.\n- **Quick-scan (qscan).** A fast, unrolled scan of many cells right at the start of the\n  round.\n  - It catches an opponent before the opponent has booted or replicated.\n  - When it finds nothing, it hands over to the main warrior.\n- **Vampire.** Bombs with `JMP` \"fangs\" that redirect enemy processes into a pit that\n  makes them harmless or useful.\n- **P-space switcher.** Uses the private p-space memory, which persists between the\n  rounds of a battle, to pick a strategy in each round from earlier results. {"type":"text","timestamp":1794660469069,"sessionID":"ses_e25f2827dffefpxLNFMrOG8SJ1","part":{"id":"prt_1da198946001R3yTO4ARBMJ6iJ","messageID":"msg_1da19671e001G3NHTXZpCkPE1Y","sessionID":"ses_e25f2827dffefpxLNFMrOG8SJ1","type":"text","text":"I've submitted a paper (self-copying) warrior called \"Mulberry\". It scores **0.390** against all 30 sparring warriors at 500 rounds. If the hidden hill behaves the same way, that is a reward of about **0.72**, where Dwarf's 0.1475 is 0 and 0.4866 is 1. The sparring warriors aren't on the hill, so the real score will differ somewhat.\n\n```\n;redcode-94\n;name Mulberry\n;author anon\n;assert CORESIZE==8000\n        spl 1, <-200\n        spl 1, <-200\n        spl 1, <-200\ns1      spl @0, }5593\n        mov }s1, >s1\ns2      spl @0, }565\n        mov }s2, >s2\ns3      spl @0, }2172\n        mov }s3, >s3\n        mov.i #1, {374\n        mov s3+1, <1178\n        jmp s3, <1420\n```\n\n**How it works:** three `spl 1` lines start 8 processes. Each copy runs a 3-stage \"silk\" copier: `spl @0` / `mov }` pairs that spread new copies across the core. Each copy then drops one anti-imp bomb, scatters fragments of its own copier code and keeps a decrement stream running.\n\n**How I picked it:**\n- **Constants:** I tried about 200 random sets of copy distances and bomb offsets at 100 rounds each, then re-ran the top 20 at 300 rounds. Nearly all of them land between 0.37 and 0.39, so the result is not very sensitive to the exact numbers. I chose the best set and confirmed it at 500 rounds.\n- **Alternatives that did worse:**\n\n| Version | Sparring score |\n|---|---|\n| Submitted paper | 0.390 |\n| Stone/imp bomber | 0.337 |\n| Switcher (uses saved results between rounds to alternate paper and stone after a loss) | 0.361 |\n| My scanners | under 0.19 |\n| Paper variants (DAT bombs, a 4th copier stage, 16 processes) | 0.365–0.386 |\n\n**Main weakness:** it ties a lot, usually 100–190 rounds out of 200 against many opponents. It survives well but rarely kills. A quick-scan opening or a core clear could turn some of those ties into wins, but I ran out of time to build either.\n\nIt's the active submission on the server, and the same code is saved in `/app/submission.red`.","time":{"start":1794660469062,"end":1794660469067}}}
